static_traits.name: Li Ran
static_traits.medical_history: Never had similar problems; never received psychotherapy or counseling; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to Reflect on own experiences, Good cooperation, slightly tense emotions

basic_info.main_problem: 'I feel terrible when dancing with my dance partner, a terrible dance partner; this belief makes me feel not good enough and has affected my enjoyment of dancing.'
basic_info.core_demands: 'I decided to seek counseling because I noticed my negative self-perception when dancing is affecting my overall enjoyment of an activity I love.'

core_beliefs: I am a terrible dance partner

special_situations.event: When practicing or performing dance with a partner, makes mistakes or takes wrong steps
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make a mistake in dancing, it means I am a bad dance partner, and I have disappointed the other party
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: To avoid disappointing the other party, gradually avoids dancing with the dance partner
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am a terrible dance partner / I will mess up again

special_situations.event: Receives positive feedback and encouragement from dance partners or others
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Positive feedback cannot prove I performed well; they are just being polite
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive feedback and practicing harder to try to prove oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite/not really thinking I dance well

special_situations.event: Dances in front of dance partners and feels the need to perform well
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot perform perfectly in front of my dance partner, I will disappoint them and damage the relationship
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Putting great pressure on oneself to pursue perfection in front of the dance partner, while not communicating true feelings with the partner
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He/she will think I am not worthy of being their dance partner

special_situations.event: Arranged or anticipating the next dance practice with the dance partner
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot guarantee no mistakes, then do not go, otherwise it will only be worse
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids feeling disappointment and shame by avoiding dancing with the dance partner
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Going will only make things worse

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen as a competent and accepted dance partner, able to enjoy dancing at ease
core_conflict.fear: Fears disappointing the dance partner, negative evaluation, damaged relationship
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being negated by Avoiding dancing with one's partner
Pressures herself to pursue perfection in front of her dance partner to control mistakes

object_relations.object_representation: Others who will be disappointed in and evaluate me

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked about the severity of the problem or whether she has communicated with others (dance partner/friends)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes that speaking out about distress seems like making a fuss or embarrassing, thus downplaying the problem
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gentle tone, affirming their feelings, inviting concrete descriptions of impact and emotional intensity; use open-ended Questioning, avoiding confrontation, encouraging reframing 'this should not be a big problem' as 'what does this mean to me'.

manifestations: Not discussing one's not-good-enough feelings and pressure with the dance partner or friends
Dancing, once loved, becomes a source of stress; enjoyment drops markedly

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequently criticizes herself as 'I am a terrible dance partner'
Fearing disappointing the other and not daring to express true needs

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves.
manifestations: Not talking about unease and shame with the dance partner or friends
Internalizing pressure and disappointment into Self-denial and avoidance behaviors

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact.
manifestations: Downplaying distress and emotional intensity with 'this is just dancing, it should not be a big problem'

exception_events.target_problem: In scenes of dancing with a partner, the client usually becomes nervous and treats mistakes as evidence that they are 'terrible', then avoids dancing with a partner.
exception_events.unique_outcome: On some 'better state' days, the client can remember the moves and be more in sync with the dance partner; when mistakes occur, can laugh them off and keep dancing, with stress markedly reduced.
exception_events.reason: Different understanding and approach: treating mistakes as tolerable Learning opportunities, not overly letting mistakes bother oneself, thus showing a deviation of better synchrony and continued practice.

positive_force: Love for dance and willingness to participate
There are 'good days' and in-sync experiences; able to laugh it off when making mistakes
Willing to seek professional help and cooperate with counseling
Has received positive feedback and invested practice
negative_force: Self-denial and Catastrophizing, easily generalizing individual mistakes into overall failure
Negating positive feedback, over-caring about others' evaluations (mind-reading, mental filtering)
Worry about disappointing the dance partner leads to avoidance and rising stress

antecedent: Arranging practice with her dance partner or anticipating the next dance
Making mistakes or wrong steps in dance
target_behavior.core_reason: Viewing individual mistakes as overall incompetence, fearing disappointing the other and being negatively evaluated (catastrophizing, overgeneralization, mind-reading)
target_behavior.function: Escaping shame and pressure, avoiding being negated and disappointing the other
target_behavior.consequence: Relationship with the dance partner is affected; enjoyment of dancing clearly declines; activity participation decreases
